title: The Hero's Journey: Campbell's Universal Pattern
description: A scholar's book, a word stolen from a novel, and a galaxy far, far away—five steps into the story behind stories.

questions.question: What 1949 book by Joseph Campbell introduced the Hero's Journey?
questions.answer: The Hero with a Thousand Faces
acceptedAnswers: The Hero with a Thousand Faces
the hero with a thousand faces
questions.explanation: Campbell compared myths from every continent and argued that their heroes follow one shared path: departure, initiation, return.

questions.question: In The Hero with a Thousand Faces, what one-word term does Campbell use for that universal pattern?
questions.explanation: One story, endlessly retold—Campbell said the hero 'ventures forth from the world of common day into a region of supernatural wonder.'

questions.question: Campbell borrowed the word 'monomyth' from which James Joyce novel?
questions.explanation: Campbell was a Joyce scholar—he co-wrote 'A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake' in 1944, five years before his own book.

questions.question: From a Finnegans Wake scholar to a movie muse: which filmmaker credited Campbell's book with shaping Star Wars?
questions.explanation: Lucas read Campbell while drafting Star Wars and later called him 'my Yoda.' Luke Skywalker's arc follows the monomyth beat for beat.

questions.question: George Lucas hosted Campbell's famous 'Power of Myth' interviews with Bill Moyers at what California property?
questions.explanation: Moyers taped five of the six episodes at the ranch over Campbell's last two summers. The series aired in 1988, the year after he died.
